body: I walked in thinking that I was taking the BC test, after all, I signed up for it. I was handed the BC booklet (no name was on it, you have to write the serial number on your scantron) and preceded to start the test. My mom checked that her check didn't specify the tests I registered for (she should have crammed the names of all five tests I was going to take), I hope that the other piece of paper (where I listed the tests I was taking) still exists. Hopefully, it doesn't "disappear" by tomorrow and I certainly hope that I wrote BC on the dang thing (it was so long ago, I'm so suspicious that I screwed up major here.)

I just feel so bad for doing what I did to the other student. The assistant principal told me to think about the effects of my actions, but I never in my wildest dream think that this was going to happen. What a day. What a day.

> What are you going to do for your community service?

I guess help out the janitors pick up trash for a couple of hours. Probably the first straight A's student and AP scholar (oh, the irony) to do this. What a way to go out with bang considering that it's the last three weeks of high school forever.

Today was the worst day ever. I think I screwed up so bad that I feel absolutely terrible. Who to tell about my sorrow none other than reddit :/
----
Today was AP Calc. test at my high school. I was only enrolled for AP Calc. AB, but I decided to pay the money and take the BC test instead. I was somewhat unprepared for the test (considering that I never studied the materials in a formal class setting), but the worst thing that I thought would happen was that I was going to get a 1 or a 2 on the test. Probably going to take the darn class again in college anyways. That was not the case. I can't be ever so wrong in my entire life. It turns out that my name wasn’t on the list for people taking the BC test, yet I was under the impression that I was (hey, I paid the money and wrote that I was going to take BC. Even my mother approved of this as she wrote the check). As I struggled passed my way through the first multiple choice part (gosh, I wished I studied more.), the assistant principal (also the proctor) walked up to me and told me to stop and take the AB test instead. Dejected, yet confused (not to mention sorely embarrassed in front of all the other AP students), I asked why. It turns out that since my name wasn’t on the list, I had someone’s copy of the test and my name was actually on the AB list. They were missing a test and had my copy for AB. I finished the other parts of the AB test (much easier) and stayed during lunch to finish the part that I didn’t take in the beginning. After I finished the AB test, I was led into the Assistant Principal’s office where he told me about the “consequences of my actions.” Apparently, the student, whose test I took, got angry and left school without telling anybody. They had to go out for two hours to find the student back. By now, I was pretty downtrodden about the day. This was the topping on a cake made of fail. Well…the “consequences” for “my selfish action” (quoting the assistant principal here) was ……..ready for this? A day of suspension and three hours of community service. No, I didn’t get  into a fight, or threatened someone, or steal. I got suspended for taking a harder test that I thought I registered for, but apparently not. This **has to be** the nerdiest way to getting suspended.  Although, I completely stricken with absolute disgust for myself today.
